content:
Curious what packages folks are using to get the most seamless lean experience in Emacs currently?

Thought I would also post what I landed on after a few months of trying different packages in the hopes that it might help someone jumping into lean editing in Emacs.

The main friction I experienced with the "official" leanprover-community emacs package was the lack of hover-docs in the info-view, but believe @Paul Nelson fixes this in his fork based on @Richard Copley eglot based fork, and so big thanks to both! I still haven't gotten recursive hover-docs working quite right with eldoc, this might be user error, is there a nice way of doing this?

After switching to this fork the next big problem I had was that the key chord package used with evil emacs for vim bindings conflicts with the quail based unicode completion used in lean4-mode and so I needed to turn off quail which I accomplished with a bit of a hack. I then replaced the quail completion with company-mode based completion using symbols from company-math, which seems to work well enough. Using company-mode I was also able to get "IntelliSense"-style completions for theorems using company-capf followed by company-dabbreva rough edge was I needed to set (setq eglot-stay-out-of '(company)) to get company-mode working properly with eglot.

One other minor problem I had was that I could not get the flymake-show-buffer-diagnosticsto work and so my collaborator @George H. Seelinger and I "vibe coded" a small fix in this fork, but I do not recommend anyone use this. Instead a feature like this maybe could be upstreamed into one of those other forks?

Another thing that made the experience better when using the lsp-mode version was setting Emacs to start lean with more memory, to do this I overwrote lean4--server-cmd here , not sure if this is the best way to do this, but the original function did not seem to pass in the arguments.

If anyone is interested my config is here.

Hope these notes help someone and wanted to say thanks again to everyone here who have made lean in Emacs more usable and fun!
